chapter: Banjo career, Armstrong and the Liberty Bell
title: Big Eye Louis, Buddy Christian and a recent carnival-day job
summary: Vincent says he played with Big Eye Louis but did not know his father. He tells of a recent carnival job with a young sax player, and says Buddy Christian played house parties and learned chords by guiding other players' fingers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Ask him, did he know Big Eye Louis?
Did you know Big Eye Louis? Oh yeah. I had to play with him sometime.
Didn't know his father. Did you know his father?

Did you know his father? Oh, what you mean, chronically? Yeah. Yeah. No, I didn't know Big Eye Louis. I didn't know his daddy. Then I got another Big Eye Louis Robinson piano player. Just told about him, eh? Yeah. Yeah. He was good, but he used to say he played too long like a woman, you know. But when I came up to learn, he wasn't much. He was good in his days. All them fellas were getting, just like if I come out that night, and he's young, she's good. They say I was good in my days, I can't make it these days. You see? But they're playing different from us, you see now. The younger generation. So about five years ago, I played with a saxophone for a drum, bounce, and a sack. And if I knew what he was blowing on that sack, nobody would know. And I did a little, did a little, did a little, did a little, and he jumped up. I said, what are you playing? He said, let's keep it hitting like I'm doing. You know, I got a good job, that night that fella was in there, and it was carnival day, it was two days old. And then one piece, I picked, you know, and then I complimented, and he tried to pot it. And that's why them fellas come and hired me that day. And man, you talk about a good little band. I told him, I said, you hear this fella play last night? He said, yeah. He said, you wasn't playing nothing with it. I said, no, indeed. I said, I wasn't doing anything, but it didn't. I said, I'm surprised to see you fellas come and hired me. And when they played, boy, them fellas played all chords. I said, that's the way I like to play with man. All know that part, chords, harmonize together. Well, we played. We didn't play no, we didn't play but three hours. We got, we got $15 an hour. And this thing's about three hours. It sprinkled a bit, but it didn't hurt us. I don't know what was the matter with the people. They followed the parade, and then when they got to Napoleon Avenue, they pulled out, and went right back to the place. It was about two hours. We stayed there about an hour. They drinking it. It was easy to stay for a while now. I've been there for a long time. It made nothing sense. Ask him who Buddy Christian played with. Did he ever play with a band? Did Buddy Christian ever play with a band? Who did he play with? I don't think Buddy Christian was just a man going around playing house party. Me and him used to do the same thing, because I was a young guy, school guy. We could play music and sit down. Yeah. And me asked them what they make. They didn't know the chords. But they were called, they said, I'm making G, E, and F. I make it on my guitar, you know. Then I catch it. But Buddy would stand over them, and when they make the chords, Buddy would move their fingers and put his hand out there. That's how he makes. That's where Buddy got so perfect. But he learned how to read, though. Just like me, you know. But most of me, Buddy, he's going to get the compliments.
